questions.question: When a fuel undergoes combustion, how does it primarily transfer energy to its environment?
options: By heating its surroundings
By cooling its surroundings
By absorbing thermal energy
By magnetic radiation

questions.question: Which laboratory method is used to compare the amounts of energy transferred by different fuels?
options: Measuring the volume of gas released during combustion
Heating water in a boiling tube and comparing the temperature changes
Weighing the ash remaining after burning
Measuring the height of the flame produced

questions.question: To ensure a fair test when comparing the energy output of different fuels, what must be kept identical for each fuel sample?
options: The shape of the container storing the fuel
The color and smell of the fuel
The mass of the fuel used for each measurement
The time of day the fuel is burned

questions.question: In a fuel-comparison experiment using heated water, what variables regarding the water must be kept constant?
options: Its boiling point and chemical formula
Its starting temperature and volume
Its density and state of matter only
Its mass and purity only

questions.question: How do state changes appear on a cooling curve graph of a substance?
options: As steep downward diagonal lines
As sharp, vertical drops
As flat, horizontal plateaus
As sudden upward spikes

questions.question: What happens when a substance cools down and undergoes a physical change?
options: It absorbs energy from the surroundings and may melt or boil
It transfers energy into the surroundings by heating and may condense or freeze
It maintains constant internal energy and may evaporate
It creates new energy and may sublime

questions.question: What temperature change is observed in the surroundings during an exothermic chemical reaction?
options: The temperature decreases
The temperature remains completely unchanged
The temperature increases
The temperature drops to freezing point

questions.question: If a chemical reaction in a beaker is endothermic, what happens to the temperature of the surroundings?
options: It increases
It decreases
It fluctuates wildly up and down
It stays exactly at room temperature

questions.question: In an exothermic reaction, how is energy transferred between the system and its surroundings?
options: Energy is transferred from the surroundings to the products
Energy is transferred from the reactants to the surroundings
Energy is created directly inside the products
Energy is destroyed within the reactants

questions.question: How is energy transferred during an endothermic chemical reaction?
options: From the surroundings to the products
From the reactants to the surroundings
From the products to the surroundings
From the container to the air only

questions.question: Which set of phase changes consists entirely of endothermic processes?
options: Condensing, freezing, and melting
Freezing, condensing, and evaporating
Melting, evaporation, and boiling
Boiling, condensing, and freezing

questions.question: Which changes of state release energy to the surroundings and are therefore classified as exothermic?
options: Melting and evaporating
Condensing and freezing
Boiling and melting
Subliming and evaporating

questions.question: Which renewable sources generate more than half of the UK's electricity?
options: Geothermal, biomass, and tidal power
Nuclear, coal, and oil
The Sun, wind, and falling water
Natural gas, wave power, and wood

questions.question: How is electricity produced using steam in a typical power station?
options: Moving steam pushes turbines, which drive electric generators
Steam directly heats the generator to create electricity
Turbines heat the water to create steam, which powers the generator
Generators spin the turbines, which turns steam back into water

questions.question: What is the current status of fossil fuels used in UK power stations?
options: Coal and oil are used, while natural gas has been completely banned
Natural gas and oil are used, but coal is no longer used
Only coal and natural gas are used; oil is never used
All fossil fuels, including coal, oil, and gas, are used equally

questions.question: Which of these fuels release both greenhouse gases and pollutants when they are burned?
options: Natural gas, oil, waste, and wood
Wind, solar, falling water, and waves
Hydrogen, oxygen, and nitrogen gases
Geothermal heat, tidal energy, and uranium

questions.question: Why are renewable energy resources considered inexhaustible and unable to run out?
options: They are artificial and can be manufactured in a lab
They are replenished more quickly than they are used up
They do not release any energy when utilized
They exist in infinite quantities deep inside the Earth's core

questions.question: Which of the following electricity-generating devices functions without using an electric generator?
options: Wind turbines
Hydroelectric dams
Steam-driven turbines
Solar panels
